say: SPIN was developed by Neil Rackham and the Huthwaite team after observing more than 35,000 business-to-business sales interactions.
Situation questions find facts you could not research. Keep them few, because they bore senior people.
Problem questions find difficulties. Where does the current setup cause the most trouble?
Implication questions explore the consequences. They are the heart of a complex sale, because most buyers have never added up what a problem costs.
Need-payoff questions let the buyer say what solving it would be worth. When they work out the cost themselves, the figure belongs to them.
For example, Halima sells IT support. At Hospital B, the IT officer says the system goes down about 3 times a month, for about 4 hours each time.

say: Implication questions help buyers see real costs. Never use them to frighten people. A case built on inflated numbers collapses when finance checks it.
Within 24 hours, send a written recap and invite corrections.

panel.heading: Putting a number on outages
items: Down about 3 times a month, 4 hours each
panel.rule: Never inflate numbers. If the buyer's estimate is small, accept it.

say: Finance looks for three numbers: total cost, return on investment, and payback.
For example, Halima proposes 350,000 naira a month, plus a one-time setup of 600,000.
Year one costs 4,800,000 naira.
The benefits, using the hospital's own estimates, are recovered billing, fewer emergency callouts, and less overtime. Together, about 5,880,000 naira.
That is a net gain of 1,080,000 naira, a return of 22.5%. Payback comes during month 5.
She also shows a cautious case. If only 40% of billing is recovered, year one shows a loss. Showing that honestly made her proposal more credible, not less.
Before negotiating, write your BATNA, your best alternative if this deal fails, plus your ideal outcome and walk-away point.
Procurement asks Halima for 10% off. Over a year that is 420,000 naira given away for nothing.
Instead she asks what is driving the request. The budget line is tight. So she offers 5% off, if the hospital signs for 24 months and pays within 14 days.
Procurement gets a saving to report, and Halima gets two years of work and faster payment.
Stay clean in procurement. Never offer gifts, cash or a percentage to anyone to influence a purchase, and walk away if one is requested.

say: On-target earnings are base pay plus target commission. For example, Bisi is offered 400,000 naira base and 200,000 target commission a month. That is 600,000 naira a month.
